s170_priorities_archived.check_method: FOG OF WAR, FOURTH AND CORRECT ATTEMPT - per-entity CULLING, the C&C model. Owner: "look at Red Alert. Theyre, like, from the fucking nineties. They did it fine." The classic model is 3 parts and this repo already had 2: the explored grid (exploredMemory -> dark/dim/clear tiers) and remembered last-seen buildings (S60 ghosts). The missing third - units in non-visible cells are simply NOT DRAWN - was the entire complaint. render/concealment.ts computes vision ONCE per frame (beginConcealmentFrame; the sources walk is O(own prims + creatures) so per-entity would be quadratic) and isConcealed(x,y,owner) is a cheap read, wired into all 10 renderers that draw his hide-list. Own entities never concealed (owner check before geometry). Bond hidden unless BOTH ends visible. structureRenderer skips BEFORE seen.add so leaving vision REAPS the sprite. Gatherer cull is in the unit loop only, because that renderer also draws the CASTLE (his one always-visible exception). "until they are in the center which is lit" needed no special case - the spawner disc is already a permanent vision source for every seat. ALSO IN P1: groundLayer at stage bottom so the 0.55-alpha backdrop stops compositing over sparks/bonds/primitives (the S166 report, live through two prior "fixes"); border walls restored to visible (R162); own-zone full-rect erase so your quadrant is lit corner to corner, not just around structures. THREE MECHANISMS WERE TRIED AND REMOVED: backdrop above the sheet (S166 class), below it (S169 class), and an inverse Pixi mask - the last shipped twice concealing nothing, first because the mask texture was tinted FOG_COLOR (a Pixi alpha mask samples a colour CHANNEL and the red channel of black is 0 everywhere), then because the mechanism was UNTESTABLE (Pixi implements alpha masks as filters; renderer.extract does not apply filter effects, so no assertion in the repo could see whether the board was concealed). Untestability was the real defect. Culling is a pure predicate: 12 tests incl. "the fog closes behind you when the spark leaves" (which forbids sticky concealment - remembering WHERE buildings were is the ghost layer, not this predicate) and "nothing concealed during FIGHT" (R62).

priorities.check_method: TOWER HEALTH BARS, POOL SEMANTICS PER HIS RULING THIS SESSION. A tower is skipped by the defender loop at `stats === null` because owner R75 gives it no pool of its own - its durability lives in the CONNECTORS. So the bar is DERIVED, not read: MAX = structureDefenceFifths(n) = n x (n+4), CURRENT = max minus the accumulated Bond.damageFifths over the component. BOTH HALVES WERE ALREADY WRITTEN AND ONE HAD NO CALLER: structureDefenceFifths (stats.ts:236) existed with ZERO production callers and its own docblock says it exists "so the HUD and the tests can speak their language" - written FOR this readout and never wired, the S167 t3TowerAtlasBase shape exactly. ZERO WIRE COST, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED: Bond.damageFifths is already serialized (save.ts:402 type, :1832 emit-when-non-zero) and already hashed (stateHashFull.ts:269 union, :538 :dmg projection), so a peer sees the true number. No new field, no protocol bump (still 46), no four-sites work. ONE BAR PER STRUCTURE, NOT PER TOWER: a pool belongs to a connected component - connectorCapacityFifths reads the CURRENT component count, so two towers welded into one lattice genuinely share one pool. Deduped by the component LOWEST primitive id, which is deterministic whichever member we enter through (Map iteration order must never decide anything in this codebase). IT COVERS TWO MAPS, AND MISSING THE SECOND WOULD HAVE LOOKED DONE: world.defenders holds only turret + stinkTower with a null pool; the GOBLIN TOWER in his screenshot is a world.creatureSpawners entry, as are the pentagram, the lightning hub, the six race towers and the six tier-9 boss towers. His words: "Also, we're gonna add a little micro priority to this session ... Add this to this session priority batch." Approval is explicit and in his own message, so no separate go was sought. Ordered AFTER P1 because both touch HUD readouts and P1 is the outstanding item from S172; P4 is independent of it and could move earlier if he prefers.

P5 ADDED MID-SESSION BY THE OWNER (second amendment this session), recorded rather than executed ad-hoc per Rule 16. His words: "we'll add this too as a micro batch to this priority... to this session." Three parts, all in the codex. ORDERING NOTE: P5(a) is a deletion and is the cheapest; P5(b) is a contained scroll container; P5(c) is the only part with real unknown cost because it needs each combo's LIVE appearance, and the combo visuals are drawn by the board renderers rather than by anything the codex can call today.

owner_questions_open_s173: VOLTKIN'S FATE IN THE CODEX - the one ambiguity in amendment 2, and it changes what ships. He said BOTH "remove the whole godly combos" AND "[Voltkin] is no more godly as anything else. It's just a tower now and structure." Reading A: delete the tab and let Voltkin appear under TOWERS & STRUCTURES (where a tower/structure belongs by his own sentence). Reading B: delete the tab and Voltkin with it, so Voltkin has no codex entry at all. NONET is NOT ambiguous - he was explicit that it must not appear anywhere in the codex because it is an Easter egg. DEFAULT IF HE DOES NOT ANSWER: Reading A, because his own words call Voltkin a tower and structure, and silently deleting a live buildable from the codex would be a bigger change than he asked for.
findings_s173: P1 CAVEAT, FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING AND NOT SWEPT: a tower can be destroyed by TWO independent damage channels, not one. (1) CONNECTORS - damageConnector accumulates Bond.damageFifths until it reaches connectorCapacityFifths(n), then the caller dispatches SEVER_BOND (damage.ts:279). (2) PRIMITIVES - damageEntity({kind:"primitive"}) does prim.hp -= amount and at zero calls razePrimitives, which takes the shape AND its incident bonds out (damage.ts:153-170); Primitive.hp is a real required field seeded at PRIMITIVE_MAX_HP = 1000 (primitive.ts:97,128). towerRenderer already derives its intact/damaged/destroyed FRAME from that second model via towerHpFrac (towerFrames.ts:190). The owner ruled the bar on CONNECTORS in his own words ("before their first connector dies") and chose POOL semantics, so that is what ships - but the primitive-hp channel is documented AT THE CONSTANT rather than left for a future session to discover the bar under-reporting. Flagged to the owner.
parallel_execution_s173: OWNER DIRECTED PARALLEL EXECUTION: "send out, like, two agents to do some other priorities ... one agent to do that [the tower shape shortfall]. NoNet, so the Sudoku, another agent to make sure the music is back, and another agent to do the codex. So three agents while you're working on priority one." AND: "we might hit limit ... so make sure to save every step ... even if we do hit limit ... you'll be able to continue exactly where we left off without losing any progress." => COMMIT AFTER EVERY GREEN STEP is an explicit owner instruction this session, and it coincides with the standing CLAUDE.md rule that protection against a full window is COMMIT FREQUENCY, not stopping early. DISPATCHED AS THREE SEPARATE Agent INVOCATIONS, deliberately NOT one workflow: the A.0 sweep earlier this session lost 6 of 8 agents to a single org spend-limit hit because all six lanes rode one invocation - the S161 failure the project CLAUDE.md warns about. Separate invocations mean a limit costs one lane. FILE OWNERSHIP, to keep three agents off each other: P4 agent owns castlePanel.ts; P6 agent owns audioManager.ts; P5 agent owns codexOverlay/codexPresentation/codexStore/comboCodexStore AND main.ts; I own healthBar.ts. P1 turned out to need NO main.ts change, which is what freed that file for the codex agent. The P4 and P6 agents were told to REPORT any main.ts edit they need rather than making it.
